only_in_confusable: [untitled BTM module] These genes sketch a morphogen-driven programme that patterns mesenchymal tissue and steers progenitors toward bone, cartilage, skin and blood-supporting fates. BMP signalling sits at its centre: SMAD1 carries the receptor signal to the nucleus, ZNF521 acts as a nuclear cofactor tuning that output in skeletal and haematopoietic progenitors, while secreted GREM1 antagonises BMP ligands to keep niches permissive, and INHBA contributes an activin/TGF-beta arm through its own receptor-SMAD route.

[untitled BTM module] This grouping centres on TGF-β/BMP superfamily signalling and its downstream control of cell fate and growth arrest. BMP4 and the activin-like receptor ACVR1C transmit ligand binding into Smad-dependent transcription, with the repulsive guidance molecule RGMA acting as a BMP co-receptor, while CDKN2B encodes the p15 cyclin-dependent kinase inhibitor that enforces the cytostatic response to these ligands in epithelial and haematopoietic cells.
[untitled BTM module] This grouping centres on adaptor and scaffold proteins that set the gain of growth-factor and inflammatory signalling rather than carrying it themselves. Two arms dominate.
